release: On demand. The four held-out upper halves and four lower halves supply four cases each. The editorial requirement is nine of ten in each group. The ten exclusions supply nine defensible decisions. Public Engineering publication and a global model budget await more evidence.
paired_comparison: Each comparison uses its own seven-day saved edition. Exact paper IDs, source, primary and secondary categories, relevance, DOI, URL, date, original title, byline and abstract matched before and after. Saved embedding and index files matched byte for byte. Initial candidate membership and review keys matched. Existing successful first-stage decisions matched exactly. Previously failed first-stage calls remained eligible for another attempt. Every second-stage result was checked against the complete proposed membership, paper-specific source offsets and downstream dated synthesis receipt. The comparison did not change the ranking formula.

matched_revised_ranks.headline: Simulated AI workload coordination cuts interconnection needs and grid costs

calibration.assessment: The profit-and-temperature study left the set. The three remaining works still study interconnection capacity, grid operating costs and an operator’s electricity bill. The power-flow paper uses benchmark GPU measurements as simulation inputs. The shared workload theme does not establish one engineering result. The revised English reader withdraws this entry.

matched_revised_ranks.headline: Equilibrium proofs and distributed solvers for prosumer and DER aggregator markets

calibration.assessment: The three papers each characterize or compute a distributed energy-market equilibrium. The revision separates an existence and uniqueness proof, convergence rates for a pricing algorithm and a learned solver that retains convergence. Those results are attributed to the studies that established them.

independent_sample.selection: Four reserved dates in chronological rotation. Each retained set appears at most once. Upper halves run from the top, lower halves from the bottom. Exclusions alternate between second-stage rejections and wholly excluded first-stage candidates. Each exclusion pool is sorted by paper IDs. All eight revised held-out ranks were examined. The grade is for the original English before editorial notes or withdrawals.

primary_check.what_was_checked: Cross-checked the original English against author abstracts, author credits, and the original methods or results where the distinction affected the grade. Source text was retrieved on November 20. Separate bylines alone do not establish independent data or replications.

high.assessment: Predicting strength from a concrete mix is a shared design task. Two teams predict compression and one predicts bending. The recycled-aggregate paper defines its most important variable as water mass divided by cement mass. Its methods say detailed binder composition was unavailable. The headline uses total binder for all three. Figure 8 confirms the water-to-cement feature ranked first in that study.

The common result concerns validation of material-property models against data splits. The concrete study reports repeated splits and source holdouts, the asphalt study reports both repeated random splits and withheld source studies, and the corbel study enumerates source partitions. Section 4.2.2 of the asphalt study confirms worse transfer to a previously unseen study. These are three different physical targets and three checks of prediction performance.

All three teams study safe control under changes in operating conditions. The first measures mission completion and tracking precision in flight. The second demonstrates lateral containment on a vehicle, and the third proves safety subject to a model-retention condition and reports hardware tests. The brief turns the first team’s improved performance into a safety result for all three.

A network capacity limit, a local service-feasibility result and oscillation attenuation are different outcomes and design tasks. The last paper studies the interaction of grid response with oscillation isolation. It does not estimate schedulable computing capacity. Ruolan Cui and Chenxi Hu appear on the first two bylines. A third similar name has different spelling and was not counted.

low.assessment: The common design question is how binder composition affects durability. Only the additive experiment measured sulfate and chloride resistance while varying dosage. The sludge review’s frequently reported optimum mainly concerns mechanical properties. The 48-study review found insufficient long-term durability evidence. The synthesis attributes a common dose-response to all three.

Each team studies predictive collision avoidance. Section 7 in the decentralized shielding manuscript reports two simulated multi-agent tasks. Its abstract omits the evaluation and the brief says the paper reports no data. The other teams report conditional safety results, hardware tests and empirical collision outcomes.

All three concern uncertainty in identification of a linear dynamical system. The source-specific outputs are eigenvalue variance, conditions for separate identification with a zero-noise convergence result, and a frequency-response error bound under assumptions. The synthesis assigns each mathematical statement and numerical check to the right team.

The studies report different theoretical and simulated outcomes. A theorem about a mathematical game, a collision-avoidance evaluation and a comparative simulation do not demonstrate the same outcome. The simulator comparison does not establish the guarantee claimed for the set.

excluded.assessment: The papers treat convergence of an optimization method, stabilization of a polynomial system, timing of an extremum-seeking loop and equilibrium recovery under disturbances. Their proofs and numerical examples do not test a common design task for three papers.
Vehicle tracking, fleet integrity and road safety are separate endpoints on different test platforms. The three papers do not establish one shared performance result.

The studies optimize hybrid access, spectrum coexistence and energy efficiency of optical networks. Two address optical resources. The third primarily measures interference-related collisions and preserved throughput.
Annual home energy and comfort, airport fleet availability and charging, and citywide travel time and emissions lead to different control decisions, measured at different scales.
The four studies report on network coordination, risk assessment, controller certification and system operating constraints. No three demonstrate the same measured quantity or engineering task.
Two papers estimate or aggregate electrical flexibility. The third compares regional frequency limits during dispatch. A three-study shared result is missing.

The five papers study safety under limited information, voltage regulation, controller identification, quantized data and time-bounded consensus. Related stability arguments serve different control tasks.
These are surveys of physical AI, learning for hardware design and learning-based control. They synthesize different bodies of work and supply no common test of engineering performance.

The first paper establishes a time horizon for information persistence. The other two concern abstraction of transition systems and a construction workflow. They do not supply three results for the same verification task.

All three ask how to reduce building heating or cooling demand while respecting occupants’ comfort. Two studies include physical building trials, and the Oman paper reviews published control strategies. A synthesis can state that design question and attribute results to each evidence type. Treating the review as a third field trial would be incorrect.

companion_works.evidence: Both papers examine the same planned Belgian wind farm cluster. The second compares alternative engineering models against the annual atmospheric simulation reported in the first. Both appeared in the same initial candidate. Neither qualified for a rank.
